verdict:
Microsoft Learn MCP is a strong, public, first-party server. It negotiates protocol 2025-06-18, issues a session, lists three well-described read-only tools, and returned useful documentation and code samples on every call, in well under a second. The daily AgentScout HTTP reachability check already had this listing as live (homepage and GitHub both HTTP 200, checked November 10, 2026, 7:03 AM PT).

The score is not 100. The server advertises prompts and resources, then returns empty lists for both. microsoft_docs_search does not mark its query argument as required. microsoft_docs_fetch has no outputSchema, unlike the other two tools. serverInfo is only a name and version. Those are fixable.
cover_blurb: A strong, public, first-party documentation server. Every tool call succeeded, in well under a second. A handful of schema and capability-honesty issues keep the score short of 100 — and they are fixable.

scorecard.why: Initialize HTTP 200, protocol 2025-06-18 accepted, session header set, notification accepted, 5/5 connects.
3/3 tool calls succeeded on every run. Search, fetch, and code-sample results were substantial and on-topic. Zero errors.
Connect p50 145.2 ms. Tool calls p50 272.7–515.6 ms. One notifications/initialized outlier at 551.5 ms.
Excellent titles, descriptions, annotations (readOnlyHint, idempotentHint, destructiveHint: false). Search query is not required and has "default": null. Fetch has no outputSchema.

Advertises prompts and resources with listChanged: true, but both lists are empty. serverInfo has only name and version (no title, website URL, or description). Initialize instructions themselves are excellent.

top_fixes.title: Mark query as required on microsoft_docs_search, and remove "default": null.
top_fixes.why: The property exists and is well described, but it is omitted from required and is given "default": null. A client can legally call the tool with no query. The other two tools correctly require their main argument. This is a one-line schema change that prevents empty searches.
steps: Add query to the required array, matching microsoft_code_sample_search and microsoft_docs_fetch.
Remove "default": null from the query property.
Redeploy and confirm that a call with no query is rejected.

top_fixes.title: Stop advertising empty surfaces — or fill them.
top_fixes.why: initialize capabilities include prompts.listChanged and resources.listChanged, but prompts/list and resources/list both returned empty arrays with HTTP 200. Clients may offer empty menus, or assume list-changed notifications that never matter.
steps: Decide whether prompts and resources are in scope for this server.
Option A — fill them: add one or two prompts that wrap the documented workflow (for example “Search Microsoft docs” and “Fetch a Learn page”), and/or a resource template for Learn URLs.
Option B — be honest: omit prompts and resources from initialize capabilities until there is something to list.
Redeploy and confirm that prompts/list and resources/list match the advertised capabilities.
top_fixes.effort: rough estimate: a small capability change

top_fixes.title: Add outputSchema to microsoft_docs_fetch, and enrich serverInfo.
top_fixes.why: Search and code-sample search both declare an outputSchema. Fetch is the tool that returns the largest body, and it only has unstructured content. serverInfo is only a name and version. A small metadata change makes this clearer for registries, catalogs, and typed clients.
steps: Declare an outputSchema on microsoft_docs_fetch (for example Markdown text plus the canonical URL).
Add title, websiteUrl, and a one-line description to serverInfo. A website URL here should be https://learn.microsoft.com/ (or the GitHub repo).
Optional: add icons so MCP client UIs can display the server consistently.
Redeploy and confirm typed clients can validate the fetch result.
top_fixes.effort: rough estimate: a small metadata change

further_improvements: serverInfo is thin. Only name and version. Context7, by comparison, also returns title, websiteUrl, and description on initialize. Optional icons would help MCP client UIs.

Search results are double-encoded as text. The content[0].text value is a JSON string of the same results already present in structuredContent. Harmless, but messier for clients that only read text content.
further_note: These two items did not cost as many points as the top three fixes. They are still worth fixing.
methodology: Reused AgentScout's existing daily MCP reachability result (HTTP HEAD-then-GET of the listed website and GitHub URL — this does not speak MCP).
Connected for real over Streamable HTTP: JSON-RPC initialize, then notifications/initialized, then tools/list, resources/list, and prompts/list.
Called three safe, read-only tools with harmless documentation queries. No write, send, pay, or delete tools were present or called.
Repeated initialize and the same three tool calls for five runs and took the median (p50) latency.
Linted tool schemas (descriptions, required fields, types, annotations).
out_of_scope: Authenticated or paid MCP servers (OAuth, API keys, x402).
stdio / npx servers (not needed here; this endpoint is public HTTP).
Write-path or destructive tool calls (none were offered).
Changing the AgentScout daily check, the listing page, or Microsoft's server.
disclaimer: This is a point-in-time test of a public MCP endpoint. All protocol calls were read-only. Results can change as the server is updated. The existing daily AgentScout check only requests the listed website and GitHub URL over HTTP; this report is the protocol-level step on top of that. Nothing in this sample was published, emailed, or changed on agentscouthq.com.
whats_great: Every connection and tool call succeeded on all 5 runs, and each one finished in under 1 second.
what_this_means: You can rely on this server for everyday use. It is a public Microsoft service, and every documentation search, page fetch, and code-sample lookup we ran came back successfully.
It is fast, too: connecting and every request finished in well under a second.

What holds the score at 90, not 100, is incomplete self-description. The server says it offers extra menus (prompts and resources), but both lists were empty, and two of the tool definitions are missing small but important details.
Make the three fixes listed on the cover, then book a free retest so we can show the score improving.
